_why: Runtimes that real, installed copies of this app report, but that the normal
`eas update` publish does NOT target. .github/workflows/pickup-native-ota.yml
republishes every merge to each entry here, so a live fleet can never be
silently stranded on an old bundle again.
app.json uses runtimeVersion.policy 'fingerprint' (since 2026-07-25), so the
normal publish targets a fingerprint hash. Every binary currently on the App
Store / Play was built BEFORE that switch, under policy 'appVersion', so those
phones report the marketing version '1.0.3' as their runtime and match nothing
the fingerprint publish produces.
REMOVE '1.0.3' only once a store build cut under the fingerprint policy has
fully replaced the 1.0.3 fleet — dropping it early stops those phones from
receiving any further update, which is the exact bug this file prevents.
Add an entry whenever a store build ships whose runtime the normal publish
will not match.
PENDING (2026-08-21): app.json is bumped to 1.0.4 / build 13 / versionCode 11
for the store build that fixes the stale embedded bundle. MEASURED: the
version identity is part of the fingerprint, so this bump moves the runtime
ios e4e2beee -> c24dc6b2 and android dbe20143 -> 0c74b3fd. Nothing is
stranded by it TODAY because no fingerprint build has ever shipped — no
device reports either hash.
AFTER the 1.0.4 build is submitted, add ITS runtime here (read the real
value from the EAS build page rather than trusting the hashes above, which
were computed from a pre-build tree). From then on the 1.0.4 fleet keeps
receiving OTAs even after a later bump moves the fingerprint again.
